transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Caleb (Redwood Solutions), Maya (VoyagerAI CTO), Luis (Lead ML Eng), Priya (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick discovery, quickstart path, want to try hosted API first with free credits, then evaluate Dedicated / Private for a pilot if latency/cost looks good. SOC2 and KMS mention.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir on the AE side, with Lena and Caleb from solutions. quick agenda — learn about your stack, what success looks like, and walk through our quickstart and pilot options.
[00:18] Maya (VoyagerAI): thanks, Samir. yep we want to move fast. we have a search/rerank pipeline that is very latency sensitive — 95th perc around 120 ms now for the embedding+rerank step. main question is: can we get to prod while controlling costs?
[00:37] Lena (Redwood): cool, and what's your traffic shape? batch or single request?
[00:42] Luis (VoyagerAI): mostly single-shot at inference time — spikes during product launches. throughput maybe 400 rps at peak. also some bulk embed jobs overnight.
[00:55] Samir (Redwood): great. typical flow for teams like yours is start with Redwood Hosted — self-serve API, free credits to get time-to-first-token in minutes, then if throughput/latency needs require it you can reserve Dedicated capacity or move to Private (VPC/on-prem) for data controls.
[01:13] Priya (VoyagerAI): quick question on free credits — how easy is it to sign up and get an API key? we want engineers to actually call it right away.
[01:20] Samir (Redwood): you sign up, we give you a sandbox API key and $500 in free credits typically, yeah it takes like <10 minutes to get started. our quickstart has sample curl, Python SDK, and node examples to hit text generation and embeddings. 
[01:38] Maya (VoyagerAI): is there an option to restrict the key to certain IPs or use SSO? we can't have keys lying around in dev for long.
[01:45] Caleb (Redwood): for hosted quickstart keys are ephemeral; for org accounts we support SSO/SAML + org-scoped API keys and RBAC. for Dedicated/Private you can hook into your KMS/HSM and audit logs.
[02:02] Luis (VoyagerAI): about latency — can you share numbers? we need 95th under 200ms for the rerank model at 1k tokens.
[02:10] Lena (Redwood): for our hosted variants we have model profiles; typical open LLMs on CPU-backed instances are slower but with our optimized serving runtime and GPU-backed endpoints we regularly see 95th in the 80-160ms range for 1k tokens depending on model and batching. that said exact numbers depend on model size, quantization, and batch settings.
[02:34] Maya (VoyagerAI): hm okay — what's the path to lower cost? quantize? batching?
[02:39] Lena (Redwood): yep — quantization profiles, continuous batching, and prefix/KV caching can reduce per-token compute. Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization configs based on your workload, and we can run a benchmark during the pilot.
[02:55] Luis (VoyagerAI): you mentioned KV cache earlier — is that something we have to manage?
[03:00] Caleb (Redwood): no, it's built into the runtime. it preserves prefix tokens and reduces recompute for chat-like workloads. sometimes the transcript svc mislabels it as K V cash, ha.
[03:10] Maya (VoyagerAI): security — we need SOC 2, ISO, audit logs, encryption at rest, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[03:19] Samir (Redwood): we are SOC 2 Type 2, have ISO in progress, and for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS and keep keys in your HSM. we can share our security pack and controls doc after the call.
[03:33] Priya (VoyagerAI): for Private — is there an on-prem option or only VPC? some regulated customers will require air gap eventually.
[03:40] Lena (Redwood): we offer VPC peering and on-prem packages for air-gapped installs; Private includes control plane pieces you can host. we'll share the product brief.
[03:50] Maya (VoyagerAI): deployment timeline if we wanted Dedicated right away?
[03:55] Samir (Redwood): Dedicated can be provisioned with reserved capacity — typical lead is 2-4 weeks for committed capacity depending on hardware availability; Hosted is immediate.
[04:05] Luis (VoyagerAI): pricing — how is it metered? tokens, embeddings? and what about committed pricing for Dedicated?
[04:13] Samir (Redwood): hosted is per-token and per-embedding unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit and lower per-unit costs; we can share a pricing sheet with examples based on your traffic shape.
[04:25] Maya (VoyagerAI): what's the minimum commit for Dedicated?
[04:28] Samir (Redwood): varies, but we typically see teams start with a 3-6 month commitment for predictability. I'll send numbers.
[04:36] Priya (VoyagerAI): do you support SSO onboarding for engineering teams so we can restrict access to keys during trial?
[04:41] Caleb (Redwood): yes, org accounts integrate with SSO and you can enable RBAC before issuing production keys.
[04:46] Luis (VoyagerAI): any gotchas with sample integrations? like does Redwood SDK auto-retry or do we need to wrap it?
[04:53] Lena (Redwood): SDK has retry/backoff and streaming helpers. for production we recommend our SDKs plus connection pools in the app.
[05:02] Maya (VoyagerAI): ok — for the quickstart we want to validate two things: 1) time-to-first-token for our devs — how long from signup to successful inference; 2) run a small latency benchmark against our representative workload.
[05:15] Samir (Redwood): perfect. typical time-to-first-token is under 10 minutes for the quickstart. bench can be scheduled — we can either run a Redwood-hosted benchmark or let you run scripts with our sample traffic.
[05:27] Luis (VoyagerAI): we prefer Redwood run it against a chosen model and then share the raw data so we can reproduce.
[05:33] Lena (Redwood): absolutely — we'll need sample payloads and auth. you can provide a small dataset (100-500 requests) that mirrors typical tokens and concurrency.
[05:44] Priya (VoyagerAI): for compliance we'll need the SOC/ISO docs and something about data retention and logs.
[05:50] Samir (Redwood): noted — I'll attach the security pack and SOC 2 report.
[05:55] Maya (VoyagerAI): one more — do you support model pinning and rollouts so we can A/B test?
[06:01] Caleb (Redwood): yes, rollouts and canary deploys are first-class; you can pin model versions per route and do traffic splits.
[06:08] Luis (VoyagerAI): for the pilot, is there a straight path from Hosted to Dedicated preserving config and keys?
[06:14] Lena (Redwood): yes we try to keep the control plane consistent — same route configs and API surface; you can migrate with minimal changes.
[06:22] Maya (VoyagerAI): any references or case studies for search/rerank customers?
[06:26] Samir (Redwood): we'll send a quick case study on search use cases and a benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:31] Priya (VoyagerAI): ok what do you need from us to start quickstart?
[06:34] Samir (Redwood): sign up for an org account, share the email domains for SSO, and Luis can send sample traffic for the benchmark. we'll provision free credits and a sandbox org.
[06:43] Luis (VoyagerAI): timeline wise we want to run the bench next week if possible.
[06:47] Lena (Redwood): we can do that — I'll schedule the technical demo/benchmark session and coordinate time windows.
[06:53] Samir (Redwood): i'll follow up with pricing, quickstart steps, and the security pack.
[06:57] Maya (VoyagerAI): good — also curious about fallback policies — if a model is down can you route to a cheaper variant automatically?
[07:05] Caleb (Redwood): yes, smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants is supported — you can define policies by latency and cost tiers.
[07:13] Luis (VoyagerAI): anything else on our end? i will compile the sample payloads and SSO meta.
[07:18] Maya (VoyagerAI): sounds good.
[07:20] Samir (Redwood): recap/next steps: Samir send pricing + free credits + security docs; Lena schedule 1-hr bench/demo; Luis send sample traffic and SSO info.
[07:30] Maya (VoyagerAI): thanks everyone. look forward to the bench.
[07:33] Samir (Redwood): thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had several mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash, Dedicated -> dedicate), occasional dropped punctuation and speaker overlaps.
